title: Prototype pure integer panelized GF(251) micro-kernel (615db3b9 Phase 1 route C)
description:
Phase 1 route C of the finite-field LA SOTA catch-up plan (`dev/active/615db3b9-finite-field-la-sota-plan.md` § Phase 1, item 3). Adds an explicit A/B panel-packing layer and a register-blocked AVX2 micro-kernel for GF(251) (byte / u16-fits primes), so the route can be compared against route A (in-Rust f32/FMA) and route B (optional BLAS) before route selection.

Parent epic: 026fc832. Predecessor: 615db3b9 (plan, done).

## Background

The plan's Phase 1, item 3 says: "Add explicit A/B panel packing and a register-blocked AVX2 micro-kernel for byte/word-fits-in-u16 primes. This is likely 1-2x slower than OpenBLAS but is the most appropriate long-term default if the project wants self-contained Rust kernels."

Current production Candidate C uses an AVX2 byte-packed whole-GEMM path without Goto/BLIS-style explicit panel packing. Route C explores whether moving to a packed-panel + register-blocked micro-kernel structure narrows the gap to fflas without giving up the self-contained-Rust property.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] A non-default dispatch toggle (cargo feature OR runtime debug switch) exposes the panelized integer kernel for GF(251) so it can be measured without changing default production behaviour.
- [hard] Bit-exact equality vs the existing Candidate C output at GF(251)/n in {64, 256, 1024} on canonical seeds.
- [hard] Implementation respects unsafe-isolation: any unsafe code lives exclusively in `gf2-kernels-simd`; `gf2-core` remains `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`.
- [hard] CCX-pinned 5-trial measurement at GF(251)/n in {256, 1024} on the 5900X reference host, recorded as a CSV + evidence markdown doc.
- [hard] Evidence doc records the panel dimensions (`mr × nr × kc`), register-blocking shape, packing layout, and how each was derived from public GEMM/ISA references (Goto-vandeGeijn "Anatomy" 2008; Zen 3 software optimization manual). No fflas-ffpack source or comments may be cited; the doc must show the derivation came from public references and gf2-owned prototypes.
- [hard] No regression on currently-PASSing GF(p) cells (delta ≤ 5%).
- [hard] If new SIMD source files are added under `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/`, sibling `*.asm.txt` artefacts land in the same commit (`asm-artefact-present` gate).

## Out of scope

- Changing production dispatch — route selection is the consumer task.
- Route A (in-Rust f32) or route B (BLAS).
- AVX-512 / VNNI variants — out of scope for 026fc832, routed to 7f809931.

## Notes

This route is expected (per the plan) to be 1–2× slower than OpenBLAS but is the structural fit for a self-contained Rust kernel. If it lands within 1.5× of fflas at n in {256, 1024}, it is the preferred production route per the Phase 1 decision rule.
